title: It's your boy, The Sprite Wizard back again with a new tool for us.
author: TheSpriteWizard
selftext:
For those of you who don't know me, I'm **The Sprite Wizard**, and I've taken it upon myself to make sprite creation a little less of a headache for indie developers.

Some of you might know my previous tools, [SpriteGrid](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-grid) and [SpritePress](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-press). They're still being used dozens of times a day, which is pretty cool to see. Thanks for that, by the way. It's nice knowing my little creations are out there doing some good.

Anyway, I've been locked away in my tower working on something new. A free tools for everyone to use!

**I call it the** [**SpriteForge**](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/spriteforge)**!**

It's an isometric character creator that lets you build, customize, animate, and export consistent pixel-art characters without having to draw every frame yourself.

I've stuffed the thing with hundreds of clothing and equipment pieces, 71 animations, up to 16 rendering directions, and enough customization options to make my head hurt.

I actually tried calculating every possible character combination. Lost count somewhere past 50 octillion.

Yes, octillion. With an O.

And that's before we even start changing colors. Admittedly, not every combination produces a visually distinct character, but you get the idea.

There's no generative AI involved. It's all built around 3D models, animation, and a pixel-art rendering engine. That said, I think it'll be especially useful for those of us who use AI in our development workflows but struggle with character consistency, or simply can't afford to commission an artist for every NPC and animation.

The idea is pretty simple: spend less time fighting with sprites and more time actually making your game.

I've put up a **free browser version** so everyone can use it. As with all of my tools, its free and it will stay free for as long as I am practicing the mystical arts:

[**Try SpriteForge on itch.io**](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/spriteforge)

It's still in Early Access, so I'm expecting a few gremlins to have made their way into the machinery.

If you find any bugs, have suggestions, or think something could work better, please let me know. I'm actively developing it, and feedback from other developers is worth considerably more to me than another evening arguing with my own code.

Anyway, that's enough rambling from an old wizard.

Hope it helps some of you get your games off the ground.

**— The Sprite Wizard**

https://i.redd.it/qaytqgfzj3vh1.gif

comments.author: Miyoumu
comments.body: Your idea of selling a sprite tool is by blasting people with a generic dog shit AI Slop banner?

replies.body: I’m not selling it. It’s free.

replies.author: Reign2294
replies.body: Yea, rock on man! Too many people woke up with a turd in their cereal. Keep on doing what you're doing, ignore them.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: Thanks. I’m not sure why they come here, bro.

replies.author: Reign2294
replies.body: Never underestimate the low self-esteem of the average reddit frequented, looking to send mean comments around to make themselves better.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: You’re probably right. I forgot to estimate it in the first place.

replies.author: A_Sword_Saint
replies.body: Why does it say download for $20, half off for $10, with future updates for free then?

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body:
Great question! The downloadable version is the Windows .exe. Buying it is a way to support me and help fund further development, and it includes future updates at no extra cost.

It runs offline and has some extras in it but it isn’t required. 

The browser version is completely free! It has ALL the character customization options and is available right on the itch.io page for everyone to use. No download or purchase required.

My goal is to make sprite creation easier and more accessible for indie devs, regardless of their budget. If someone wants to toss a few gold coins my way to help keep the forge burning, that's always appreciated, but certainly not required!

comments.author: hugomcjohnson
comments.body: Why is it ALWAYS pixel art only?

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: For me? Because I like Pixel Art. Do you need help with a different style? Maybe I can point you in the right direction.

replies.author: hugomcjohnson
replies.body: Im talking generally. Every single sprite generation site out there is always pixel art only, like everyone only wants to make pixel art games

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: Oh. There’s also a lot of 3D model sites. You’ve got things like Vroid that do the same thing. The more popular for game development is 2D pixel art because the art is simple to make and can portray an idea without the expensive 3D systems. 3D stuff outside of low poly is super detail focused. So for a game dev hobbyists it’s usually easier to just comply and paste some pixels rather than build some complex world. So it’s more popular.
